![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/30aa4c5e72919d09a0a2323dc8af90a73810047857f3c89fe9c3005a10c195ae.png)

Consider the finite region bounded by the curves $x=4y-{y}^{2}$ and $x=2y,$ as shown above. Find an integral expression for the volume generated when this region is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the $x$-axis.
question.worked_solution:
First, let $f(y)=4y-{y}^{2}$ and $g(y)=2y.$

We start by determining the points where the curves intersect by solving the following equation for $y:$

$$
\begin{aligned}f(y) & =g(y) \\ 4y-{y}^{2} & =2y \\ 2y-{y}^{2} & =0 \\ y(2-y) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions corresponding to our region are $y=0$ and $y=2.$ So, we need to integrate from $y=0$ to $y=2.$ 

Now, let's draw our usual horizontal arrow through the region to determine the left and right functions.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14224622/assets/cbfd6c409590e6b6d350b5ae8f6531944467e90991b17582febe228a6a8dfdb2.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the left function $x=g(y)=2y,$ and

- *leaves* through the right function $x=f(y)=4y-{y}^{2}.$

Therefore, using the shell method, the volume of the solid can be expressed as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}V & =2\pi {\int }_{c}^{d}y([\text{right}]-[\text{left}])\,\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}y([4y-{y}^{2}]-[2y])\text{d}y \\  & =2\pi {\int }_{0}^{2}y(2y-{y}^{2})\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$
